responseText:
Good — here are clear, practical layout changes I’d recommend (each with the reason) so you can decide before we render.

1) Reconsider the two photos stacked on the left
- Change: either give them more separation/overlap and different sizes, or switch to side-by-side / one large hero image.
- Why: two equal stacked photos create heavy visual weight on the left and can break the eye flow. Varying size or using one dominant image establishes a clearer focal point and looks more balanced.

2) Move or align the headline for better hierarchy
- Change: keep the headline across the top but give it more breathing room and align it either centered or left-aligned with the photos (not floating over them).
- Why: a headline that sits too close to images or the edge competes for attention. Clear alignment and space make the message instantly readable and guide the eye downward.

3) Create a clear visual path from headline → photos → CTA
- Change: use subtle rules, whitespace, or overlapping elements to lead the viewer diagonally from the headline to the photos and then to the QR/CTA.
- Why: viewers usually scan posters quickly. A designed flow increases the chance they notice and act on the QR code.

4) Add a short CTA above or immediately beside the QR
- Change: include one line like “Scan to apply” or “Join now — scan here” and position it directly adjacent to the QR.
- Why: a QR alone is ambiguous; a nearby, succinct action line makes intent clear and increases engagement.

5) Don’t put the QR flush in the corner — give it a quiet zone and background
- Change: move the QR slightly inward and place it on a light/contrasting panel or white rounded box; ensure a clear quiet zone around it.
- Why: QR codes need space and contrast to scan reliably. Corners and dark backgrounds can make scanning fail and risk being cut off in print or occluded in photos.

6) Increase contrast and tune type for a dark background
- Change: use high-contrast, slightly off-white text, increase headline weight/size, and ensure subhead text is legible (don’t use thin light fonts).
- Why: dark backgrounds can make fine text unreadable from distance. Strong contrast and robust typography maintain legibility.

7) Introduce an accent color for CTA/important elements
- Change: use a single bright accent (e.g., a warm color) for the CTA, small iconography, or a highlight bar.
- Why: a single accent guides attention to actions (like the QR) without cluttering the dark aesthetic.

8) Treat photos for cohesion
- Change: apply a consistent crop, color treatment (subtle desaturation or warm tone), or frame style (rounded corners, thin border).
- Why: different-looking images read as disconnected; consistent treatment ties the layout together and supports the brand tone.

9) Mind margins, bleed, and real-world viewing distance
- Change: keep important text and the QR well inside the safe margin (don’t rely on edge placement); size headline and QR to suit expected viewing distance.
- Why: posters get trimmed, pinned, or viewed from afar. Ensuring safe margins and appropriate sizes prevents cropping and keeps elements readable.

10) Add micro-copy for trust/credibility if needed
- Change: small line with organization name/logo, a one-line benefit, or legal/age requirement if relevant.
- Why: brief credibility cues help users trust the QR and understand purpose at a glance.

Quick tradeoff options (pick one per area)
- Photos: two stacked but varied size (modern, dynamic) OR single hero photo (clean, focused).
- Headline: full-width centered for drama OR left-aligned with photos for tighter composition.
- QR: corner with large white panel (bold, modern) OR lower-right but inset with CTA label (subtle, safe).

Pre-render checklist to confirm before we burn a render
- Poster size / intended viewing distance
- Exact headline copy and CTA text
- Which photo(s) to use and any crop preference
- QR content and confirmation that it scans (we’ll test at final size)
- Logo and color palette
- Print bleed/safe margin requirements

Tell me which choices you prefer (photo option, headline alignment, QR style) and any copy you want set, and I’ll produce a render plan matching those decisions.
